entry.title: OECD data show graduate unemployment rising for the first time since its records began
entry.summary:
The OECD's Education at a Glance 2026, launched on 29 September 2026, found that unemployment among 25 to 34 year olds with a university degree rose by 0.4 percentage points across member countries between 2023 and 2025, while unemployment among those with only upper secondary education fell by 0.2 percentage points, narrowing the usual gap and marking the first such reversal since the series began in 2000. South Korea illustrates the pattern starkly: 71.1% of its 25 to 34 year olds hold a tertiary qualification, well above the OECD average of 47.5%, yet its graduate employment rate of 80.1% trails the OECD average of 86%.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 4, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, this is the clearest OECD-wide signal yet that a degree's labour-market advantage is narrowing just as AI reshapes entry-level work, a trend Wits AHEAD should track against South Africa's own graduate destination data.

OECD, Education at a Glance 2026 (via UPI) · Intergovernmental body data, reported by an international wire service

entry.title: Côte d'Ivoire launches UNESCO-backed AI training for 3,000 vocational education teachers
entry.summary:
Côte d'Ivoire's Minister Delegate for Technical Education and Vocational Training, Jean-Louis Moulot, launched a programme on 25 September 2026 to train 3,000 vocational education teachers, pedagogical supervisors and administrators in artificial intelligence, with technical support from UNESCO. The first phase runs from 1 October to 30 December 2026, training 1,000 teachers in Abidjan in AI fundamentals, educational applications, assessment methods, ethics and data security, before the pilot is evaluated for nationwide expansion.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 3, AI and analytics in STEM and teacher education, this is a rare government-led, UNESCO-supported programme that trains the teacher-educators themselves rather than only their students, a model Wits AHEAD can draw on in its own work with South African technical and vocational colleges.

TrendsnAfrica · Government programme launch with UNESCO technical support, reported by regional press

entry.title: Ghana commits to train 100,000 TVET facilitators in AI under new UNESCO and Microsoft partnership
entry.summary:
Ghana's Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Service signed a memorandum of understanding with UNESCO, KPMG and Microsoft on 30 September 2026 to train at least 100,000 TVET facilitators in artificial intelligence and digital skills under the AI EmpowerED initiative. TVET Service director general Dr Eric Kofi Adzroe said the partnership marked a shift towards a system aligned with industry, powered by technology and focused on outcomes, while UNESCO country representative Edmond Moukala signed the agreement on the organisation's behalf.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 4, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, equipping technical and vocational instructors with AI skills at this scale could reshape how an entire generation of African artisans and technicians enters an AI reshaped labour market, a model Wits AHEAD watches for lessons applicable to South Africa's own TVET sector.

Graphic Online · National press, government partnership announcement

entry.title: US learning platform data shows AI tools trail far behind other classroom technology
entry.summary:
Instructure's new EdTech Top 40 report, based on anonymised data from 19.5 million higher education users of its Canvas learning platform between September 2025 and April 2026, found that Google Gemini, the most widely adopted dedicated AI tool, reached only 87,788 users across 211 institutions and failed to crack the top 100 integrated tools. Established tools such as McGraw Hill, with 11.3 million users, Watermark course evaluations and Zoom remained far more widely used. Instructure vice-president Ryan Lufkin said universities were signing enterprise wide AI deals without yet embedding the tools into everyday coursework.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 1, generative AI in higher education, the gap between institutional AI licensing and actual classroom use is a caution Wits AHEAD is tracking: buying access to AI tools is not the same as integrating them into teaching and assessment, and the group's own work on practical adoption speaks directly to that gap.

Inside Higher Ed · Established press report on industry usage data

entry.title: UNESCO programme trains over 100 rural teachers and principals across China and Southeast Asia in AI and STEM
entry.summary:
UNESCO reported on 30 September 2026 that its China-Southeast Asia Capacity Development Programme for Teachers and Principals, held in Beijing from 17 to 23 August 2026 under the theme 'STEM and AI: Empowering Rural Teachers for Digital Transformation', brought together over 100 education policymakers, school leaders, teachers and experts from China and Southeast Asian countries. Organised with UNESCO's International Research and Training Centre for Rural Education, SEAMEO RECSAM, the UNESCO Chair on Artificial Intelligence in Education at Beijing Normal University and the OECD, the programme focused on using AI and STEM teaching to advance digital equity in underserved rural communities. Professor Shahbaz Khan, director of UNESCO's Regional Office for East Asia, called for 'human centred, ethical and inclusive AI in education'.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 3, AI and analytics in STEM and teacher education, the programme's insistence that technology can support but never replace rural teachers offers a model Wits AHEAD can draw on for its own work preparing teacher educators across under resourced parts of the Global South.

UNESCO · Intergovernmental body

entry.title: Ethiopia's Education Ministry says AI will support, not replace, teachers as it expands digital learning
entry.summary:
Ethiopia's Minister of Education, Berhanu Nega, said on 29 September 2026 that teachers across the country are being supported to use artificial intelligence for lesson preparation, content development, student support and assessment, alongside digitalisation of the ministry's Education and Higher Education Management Information Systems. The Minister stressed that AI is being introduced to strengthen teachers' capacity rather than replace them, as part of a wider push on online, blended and micro credential learning and stronger digital connectivity for universities and schools. He called for the education system to move beyond memorisation and develop critical thinkers who can 'work together with machines'.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 1, generative AI in higher education, and pillar 5, analytics and data for education systems, a national ministry publicly committing to AI as a support for teachers rather than a replacement, alongside systems level data reform, is the kind of policy signal Wits AHEAD tracks across the Global South.

allAfrica (Ethiopian News Agency) · National press, government ministry announcement

entry.title: Africa must build its own AI solutions rather than import them, says UN scientific panel member
entry.summary:
Girmaw Abebe Tadesse, who leads Microsoft's AI for Good Lab in Kenya and sits on the United Nations' Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence, told UN News during UN High Level Week in New York on 25 September 2026 that African countries should identify their own problems before adopting technology designed elsewhere. He said stakeholders, including higher education institutions, governments, development partners and technology companies, should pool knowledge to build solutions suited to local realities rather than duplicating effort, and pointed to Africa's young population as a source of innovation already applying technology to community challenges.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 6, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, a UN scientific adviser explicitly naming universities as essential partners in a locally led AI agenda reinforces the case for Wits AHEAD's own emphasis on African owned research and solutions, not imported frameworks.

allAfrica (UN News) · UN News Service, intergovernmental body

entry.title: Cape Town hosts first African THE World Academic Summit as Wits and four other South African universities rise in the world rankings
entry.summary:
The Times Higher Education World Academic Summit opened at the University of Cape Town on 30 September 2026, the first time the event has been held on the African continent, alongside the launch of the THE World University Rankings 2027. Five South African universities now rank in the global top 500, including Wits at 301 to 325, with the University of Cape Town rising to joint 147th, its best position in seven years. UCT vice-chancellor Mosa Moshabela said the university had switched off its AI detection tools to focus on teaching students to use AI properly, while Higher Education Minister Buti Manamela noted that six in ten young South Africans are unemployed.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 1, generative AI in higher education, UCT's decision to drop AI detection in favour of teaching proper use marks a shift in assessment policy that Wits AHEAD is tracking across the sector, and the rankings rise together with the Minister's unemployment figure underline why AI, analytics and graduate capability matter for every South African university, Wits included.

Daily Maverick · Established press

entry.title: Alliance for African Partnership meets in Dar es Salaam and puts AI skills at the centre of regional cooperation

category.term: Africa (Tanzania, hosted by the University of Dar es Salaam)

entry.summary:
The Alliance for African Partnership, a consortium of 12 universities from 10 African countries anchored by Michigan State University, held its 2026 annual meeting at the University of Dar es Salaam from 16 to 22 September. Deputy Vice-Chancellor for Research Nelson Boniface told delegates that universities must update their curricula and train lecturers so that graduates are not left behind by artificial intelligence, adding that AI literacy is now a skill every student needs, not only computer scientists.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 4, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, the Alliance's call for curriculum reform and lecturer training across ten African countries echoes Wits AHEAD's own case for embedding AI literacy in every discipline, not only STEM, to keep African graduates employable.

allAfrica.com, from the Daily News (Tanzania) · Established African news service

entry.title: Morgan State University wins 10 million dollar federal grant to build a trusted AI research institute
entry.summary:
Morgan State University, a historically Black university in Baltimore, has received 10 million dollars in United States federal funding to establish the Institute for Trusted Autonomous Networks, known as TITAN, US senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks announced on 16 September 2026. The five year grant funds research and doctoral training in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and quantum enhanced security, and is intended to help Morgan State reach the highest tier of American research universities.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 3, AI and analytics in STEM and teacher education, TITAN's focus on training doctoral researchers at a historically Black university shows how targeted AI research funding can widen who leads AI research, a question Wits AHEAD tracks for equity in STEM worldwide.

CBS News Baltimore · Established press

entry.title: MIT trains faculty from other universities to teach AI across disciplines
entry.summary:
The MIT Stephen A. Schwarzman College of Computing has piloted a week long workshop that trains faculty from other colleges and universities to teach artificial intelligence and machine learning within their own subjects, adapting materials from MIT's own "Modelling with Machine Learning" course. The inaugural workshop in July 2026 brought together 19 academics from seven institutions, including Allen University, Babson College, Brandeis University and the University of Massachusetts at Lowell, with more than half a dozen MIT instructors teaching sessions spanning finance, computer science and sustainability.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 3, AI and analytics in STEM and teacher education, the pilot tackles a bottleneck Wits AHEAD also faces: academics outside computer science need practical, hands on training before they can teach AI literacy credibly within their own disciplines.

MIT News · University announcement

entry.title: UNESCO survey finds most Latin American and Caribbean universities use AI, but few have a strategy
entry.summary:
UNESCO's International Institute for Higher Education in Latin America and the Caribbean (IESALC), working with the United Nations University Institute for the Advanced Study of Sustainability, surveyed 200 higher education institutions across 19 countries and published its findings on 8 September 2026 during UNESCO's Digital Learning Week. It found that 87 per cent of institutions already use AI in at least one area of their work, most often in teaching and learning, but only 26 per cent have a formal AI strategy. Most AI initiatives start with individual academics, researchers or students rather than institutional leadership.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 6, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, the gap between near universal AI use and formal governance across Latin America and the Caribbean mirrors a pattern Wits AHEAD tracks across the Global South, where everyday practice is running ahead of institutional policy.

UNESCO IESALC and United Nations University · Intergovernmental higher education body report

entry.title: University of Colorado system adopts a living policy for responsible use of AI
entry.summary:
The University of Colorado system's new Administrative Policy Statement 6012, Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence, took effect on 24 August 2026 and was set out on the university's policy blog on 21 September. It establishes systemwide expectations for academic integrity, data protection, transparency and verifying AI-generated content for accuracy, and is explicitly presented as a policy meant to evolve as feedback comes in from students and staff.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 1, generative AI in higher education, teaching, assessment and integrity, a large public university system choosing to treat its AI rules as a living document rather than a fixed policy is a Global North comparator for the governance choices Wits AHEAD tracks in the Global South.

University of Colorado · University policy announcement

entry.title: University of Pretoria trains future teachers in "prompt literacy" for the AI classroom
entry.summary:
Researchers in the University of Pretoria's Department of Early Childhood Education, led by Dr Joyce West and Dr Kayla Willemse, are running a multi-phase study on prompt literacy, the ability to give generative AI clear instructions while critically judging what it produces. The project trains future teachers to use AI as a collaborative classroom tool rather than a threat, through activities such as building children's stories and digital materials, while keeping a close eye on bias, inaccuracy and copyright in what the AI generates.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 3, AI and analytics in STEM and teacher education, the study addresses a gap Wits AHEAD watches closely: whether new teachers are actually taught how to question AI output, not only how to produce it.

Future SA, reporting University of Pretoria research · South African higher education press, reporting university research

entry.title: East African universities and Arizona State University partner to build "AI-ready" higher education
entry.summary:
The Inter-University Council for East Africa, the East African Community's higher education body, announced a partnership on 9 September 2026 with Arizona State University's University Design Institute to help East African universities become AI-ready. The work covers four areas: leadership and governance, faculty development, research ecosystems and cross-institutional learning. The Design Institute brings experience from 26 countries and more than 140 institutions, including seven in Africa.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 5, analytics and data for education systems and decision-making, the partnership shows a regional higher education body building AI capacity across many universities at once, a model Wits AHEAD can compare against its own reach in Southern Africa.

Inter-University Council for East Africa · Intergovernmental higher education body announcement

entry.title: Maharashtra sets up a state committee to govern AI and data dashboards across its universities
entry.summary:
Maharashtra's Higher and Technical Education Department has issued a government resolution setting up an AI, Data Analytics and Dashboard Governance Committee, chaired by Professor Rajnish Kamat, vice-chancellor of Shivaji University, Kolhapur. Over its three-year term the nine-member committee must set a state AI strategy, choose priority uses for generative AI, machine learning and natural language processing, standardise data across the state's existing student, examination and scholarship dashboards, and build automated trend analysis and risk forecasting into a portal that currently only reports numbers, while meeting cybersecurity and privacy rules. It reports every quarter to the department's most senior civil servants.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 5, analytics and data for education systems and decision-making, this is one of the first state governments anywhere to put a standing, accountable committee in charge of turning a reporting dashboard into a genuine early-warning and decision-support system, a model Wits AHEAD can point to when arguing for the same shift in South Africa.

Government of Maharashtra, Higher and Technical Education Department · State government resolution, reported by regional press

entry.title: Telkom Foundation, BCX and Alibaba Cloud partner with Wits to give students AI-powered coding tools
entry.summary:
Telkom Foundation, BCX and Alibaba Cloud have partnered with the University of the Witwatersrand to give about 165 third-year Computer Science students access to Alibaba's Qoder AI-powered development platform for their academic software projects. The Qoder Programme is meant to give students hands-on experience of AI-assisted coding tools before they enter a workplace where such tools are now standard, and to strengthen the link between the Wits curriculum and industry practice. Professor Richard Klein, head of the Wits School of Computer Science and Applied Mathematics, said the curriculum needs to evolve alongside these global developments.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 4, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, this is a concrete step by Wits itself to close the gap between what computer science graduates learn and the AI-augmented software engineering roles they will enter, at a scale Wits AHEAD can track and build on.

Wits University · University announcement

entry.title: Systematic review of 124 studies finds AI's value in education depends on governance, not the technology, and flags a Global South research gap

category.term: Global (evidence base: Central Asia, East Africa)

entry.summary:
A systematic narrative review by researchers based at universities in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Tanzania synthesised 124 studies published between January 2020 and January 2026 on how artificial intelligence is reshaping education. It found a real but uneven shift from isolated AI tools towards more adaptive, data-informed teaching, and concluded that whether this shift helps or harms learners depends on governance and institutional context rather than the technology itself, and that human judgement and the teacher's role must stay central rather than treating AI as an autonomous authority. The authors also found the evidence base itself skewed heavily towards English-language scholarship, with Global South, indigenous and multilingual perspectives still largely missing.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 6, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, this is a peer-reviewed confirmation, from researchers themselves based in Central Asia and East Africa, of the exact evidence gap that motivates Wits AHEAD's own work: the literature meant to guide AI policy in education barely includes the Global South voices it should be guided by.

Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Business schools bring back oral defences as AI use rises
entry.summary:
Leading European business schools, among them Insead, Imperial College Business School and HEC Paris, are reintroducing oral defences, pen-and-paper exams and closely supervised assessment because generative AI has undermined the standard take-home case study. Imperial's Peter Todd said staff can no longer be confident what a written submission represents unless students defend it in person or write it under supervision, and HEC Paris now alternates between assessments done with computers and without them. The Graduate Management Admission Council said assessment standards need to be clearer if business qualifications are to keep their meaning.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 1, generative AI in higher education, this shows leading business schools abandoning take-home assessment altogether rather than patching it, which matters directly for how Wits AHEAD frames assessment integrity guidance for African universities facing the same pressure with far fewer resources for oral or supervised exams.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press

entry.title: African curriculum experts meet in Dar es Salaam to confront the AI challenge in teacher education
entry.summary:
The Sixth Conference of the African Curriculum Association was held in Dar es Salaam from 22 to 25 September 2026, bringing together curriculum developers, teacher trainers, researchers and policymakers from across the continent. Tanzania Institute of Education director general Dr Aneth Komba and ACA secretary general Dr Gertrude Namubiru led discussions on how African curricula and teacher preparation must adapt to artificial intelligence and rapid technological change while staying grounded in local skills and community needs. The conference set out to produce a Dar es Salaam Declaration on Education Transformation in Africa, aligned with the African Union's Agenda 2063 and the fourth Sustainable Development Goal.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 3, AI and analytics in STEM and teacher education, a continent-wide gathering setting out how teacher preparation itself must change for an AI-shaped classroom speaks directly to Wits AHEAD's work on what teacher educators need to know, not only what pupils and students should be taught.

The Citizen (Tanzania) · Established national press

entry.title: Universities must teach people to work ‘with AI, not for AI’, says King's College London head
entry.summary:
Speaking at the 2026 Korea Times Global Conference in Seoul, King's College London vice-chancellor Shitij Kapur said universities must ensure people work with artificial intelligence rather than for it. He set out five responsibilities for universities: redefining what learning means, preparing graduates for a changing labour market, protecting thoughtful scholarship, advancing AI for the collective good and making sure the technology strengthens rather than replaces human capability. Kapur argued that AI's development is not fixed, and that universities and nations can still shape how it is built and used rather than simply accepting it from the technology industry.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 6, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, a leading vice-chancellor putting universities at the centre of shaping AI rather than merely reacting to it supports Wits AHEAD's own case that higher education in the Global South should help set the terms of AI adoption, not just absorb tools built elsewhere.

University World News · Established higher education press

entry.title: Latin America's universities embrace AI faster than they can govern it, new study finds
entry.summary:
A UNESCO IESALC study of 200 higher education institutions across 19 Latin American and Caribbean countries found that 87 per cent already use artificial intelligence in some part of their work, yet only 26 per cent have any formal AI framework. Adoption is highest among private non-profit universities, at 84 per cent, against 68 per cent for public institutions and 52 per cent for private for-profit providers, and 55 per cent of universities overall have no dedicated AI budget. UNESCO's Borhene Chakroun said maximising the benefits depends on sustained investment in access and capacity, with governance that ensures ethical use, transparency and accountability.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 6, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, this shows the gap Wits AHEAD warns against taking hold at scale: public universities, which serve the students with fewest alternatives, are adopting AI fastest in the classroom while lagging furthest behind on governance, training and funding to use it responsibly.

Times Higher Education · Established higher education press, reporting a UNESCO IESALC study

entry.title: African universities can drive talent development at scale, Mastercard Foundation tells Accra convening
entry.summary:
At the inaugural Higher Education Transformation Convening in Accra on 22 September 2026, the Mastercard Foundation's Dr John Nkengasong described African universities as 'engines of prosperity' and human capital infrastructure that must align teaching with labour markets and industry. The event recognised five institutions with the Africa Higher Education for Transformation (AHEFT) Prize: Addis Ababa University, 2iE, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, Muni University and the University of Rwanda. The foundation restated its goal of helping 30 million young Africans, 70 per cent of them women, into dignified work by 2030.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 4, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, a major funder framing universities as talent infrastructure, while naming AI as a force reshaping work, strengthens the case for Wits AHEAD's evidence on which graduate capabilities actually lead to dignified work in African labour markets.

University World News · Established higher education press

entry.title: 'Syncopathy' and AI: African HE must choose verification
entry.summary:
Writing in University World News, Dr Kende Kefale of the University of Cape Town coins 'syncopathy' for AI outputs, such as citations and arguments, that look plausible but skip verification, and argues that universities share the same flaw because checking work is costly and invisible while output is cheap and easy to count. He proposes that institutions disclose how much work receives human examination before credentials are conferred, that every automated detection system have a named person accountable for its errors, and that verification records become a lasting institutional output. He points to South Africa's draft National AI Policy, withdrawn in April 2026 after fabricated citations were found in its reference list.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 6, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, the argument gives Wits AHEAD a practical frame for AI governance in African universities, one that places the cost of verification and accountability for automated judgements with institutions rather than with students.

University World News · Commentary by a University of Cape Town academic in established higher education press

entry.title: From AI use to funding cuts: how provosts are navigating 2026
entry.summary:
Inside Higher Ed's 2026 survey of 376 chief academic officers, fielded by Hanover Research, finds that about seven in ten provosts use AI in their own work at least weekly, yet only one in ten says their institution has a centralised AI strategy. Only 12 per cent report department workflow gains from institutional AI investment and 8 per cent institution-wide transformation, while 15 per cent have not invested at all. Skills and staff capacity (51 per cent) and faculty and staff resistance (50 per cent) are the main barriers cited.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 5, analytics and data for education systems and decision-making, the gap between leaders' personal use of AI and institutional strategy is exactly the space where Wits AHEAD argues for evidence-led, system-level decisions about AI in universities.

Inside Higher Ed · Established higher education press; national survey fielded by Hanover Research

entry.title: Record number of graduates pushes youth unemployment to 18.9%
entry.summary:
Urban unemployment among 16 to 24 year olds in China, excluding students, rose to 18.9 per cent in August 2026 from 17.9 per cent in July, according to National Bureau of Statistics figures reported by University World News. The rise followed a record 12.7 million university graduates this summer and is the highest reading since the methodology changed in 2023. The report points to weak domestic demand and the growing adoption of artificial intelligence as pressures on entry-level hiring.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 4, graduate capability, employability and just transitions, China's graduate squeeze shows that expanding higher education does not on its own secure entry into work when AI is reshaping entry-level roles, a lesson Wits AHEAD will weigh against graduate labour markets in South Africa and the wider Global South.

University World News (from the South China Morning Post) · Established higher education press reporting national statistics

entry.title: Ten-country African university alliance pushes joint research and AI skills
entry.summary:
The Alliance for Africa Partnership, a consortium of 12 institutions across 10 African countries anchored by Michigan State University, used its annual meeting in Dar es Salaam on 22 September 2026 to call for closer joint research and for universities to build artificial intelligence skills into their curricula. Professor Nelson Boniface of the University of Dar es Salaam told delegates that AI competency is now a basic requirement for every graduate, not only for those who code, and urged stronger links between universities, industry and government to turn research into practical problem solving.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: Pillar 4 covers AI, graduate capability, employability and just transitions. A ten-country African university alliance putting AI skills and joint research on its own agenda, without waiting for outside frameworks, is a live example of the cross-border collaboration Wits AHEAD studies and a reminder that the continent's skills gap is being addressed from within.

Tanzania Daily News, via allAfrica · African press wire service

entry.title: Report warns AI adoption in US colleges is outpacing student safeguards
entry.summary:
A new report from Student Defense's SHAPE initiative, covered by Inside Higher Ed on 18 September 2026, finds that United States colleges have woven artificial intelligence into admissions, financial aid, advising and teaching faster than they have built safeguards to protect students. It identifies algorithmic bias in aid decisions, data privacy gaps and a loss of authentic learning communities as the main risks, and calls on institutions to set clear governance and transparency rules before deploying AI systems further.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 6, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, the report is a concrete checklist of where AI governance in higher education is falling behind practice, useful for testing Wits AHEAD's own guidance on transparency and accountability against a system further down the adoption curve.

Inside Higher Ed · Established higher education press

entry.title: UNESCO: over 25 education ministers declare AI must serve the 'common good'
entry.summary:
More than 25 education ministers and senior officials meeting at UNESCO's Digital Learning Week in Paris adopted a joint statement on 8 September 2026 declaring that education must remain a human right and a common good as artificial intelligence spreads through classrooms and universities. The statement sets out eight priorities, including keeping AI systems auditable and subject to public oversight, and protecting teachers' say over classroom technology. It cited a UNESCO survey in which 93 per cent of academics believed students were using generative AI to produce assignments, and 63 per cent perceived a decline in students' cognitive capacities.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: For pillar 6, responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy, a ministerial statement of this scale gives Wits AHEAD an internationally endorsed benchmark for what public accountability in AI governance should look like, one that universities and national policymakers in the Global South can cite directly.

UNESCO · UN agency ministerial statement

entry.title: University of Alaska regents weigh a system-wide AI policy for every campus
entry.summary:
The University of Alaska's Board of Regents has reviewed a draft artificial intelligence policy that would require all three of its campuses to put in place an AI implementation plan for students, staff and faculty. The draft sets out guiding principles on preserving human judgement, protecting data privacy and security, and using AI to widen access to education services, with feedback sessions planned through autumn 2026 and final approval targeted for the November regents meeting.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: Pillar 6 covers responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy. A public university system building its AI governance from first principles, in public and with regents raising questions about monitoring capacity, is a useful governance model for Wits AHEAD to track as it develops its own policy guidance.

Alaska Public Media · Public broadcaster report

entry.title: World Bank opens free AI skills training to young people across 44 African countries
entry.summary:
The World Bank has launched 'The Job I Hope For', inviting young people aged 18 and over across 44 Sub-Saharan African countries to register for free online training in generative AI fundamentals, prompt writing and AI ethics, delivered in English and French in October 2026. The programme responds to a continent where more than 600 million young people are expected to enter the labour market by 2050, asking participants to first set out the career they hope for before building the AI skills to reach it.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: Pillar 4 covers AI, graduate capability, employability and just transitions. A continent-wide, free AI skills programme aimed squarely at youth entering the workforce is a direct test of how training at scale can be built for the labour markets Wits AHEAD studies, and a possible partner or model to watch.

World Bank · Intergovernmental body brief

entry.title: Systematic review finds AI training for future primary maths teachers is still too brief to stick
entry.summary:
A systematic review by researchers at three Portuguese universities examined 11 peer-reviewed studies on how pre-service primary school teachers are trained to use AI in mathematics teaching. Most training ran as short sessions bolted onto existing courses rather than sustained modules, and covered AI awareness and practical use well but ethics and critical evaluation only inconsistently, leaving little evidence that skills transfer into real classrooms.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: Pillar 3 covers AI and analytics in STEM and teacher education. The review's four essential dimensions, awareness, literacy and prompting, pedagogical integration and critical evaluation, give Wits AHEAD a concrete checklist for designing its own teacher-training work rather than a one-off AI workshop.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed systematic review

entry.title: New scale measures students' skill at using AI responsibly in assessed work
entry.summary:
Researchers at three institutions in China have developed and validated an eighteen-item scale that measures how well higher education students understand assessment criteria, disclose their use of AI and preserve academic integrity when using generative AI in coursework. Tested with 486 students and then a separate 798, the scale showed a reliable five-factor structure and was strongly linked to how much students engaged with feedback and their intention to act with integrity.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: Pillar 1 covers generative AI in higher education: teaching, assessment and integrity. A validated instrument like this gives institutions a practical way to measure and build students' assessment literacy, rather than relying only on detection software or blanket bans.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Prescriptive AI model flags Ecuadorian students at highest dropout risk, and what would change it
entry.summary:
Researchers at a public university in Ecuador built a prescriptive analytics framework, tracking 2,500 students who entered between 2020 and 2024, that not only predicted dropout risk with high accuracy (ROC-AUC 0.95 to 0.97) but identified the smallest feasible changes, such as an extra early credit or better home internet access, that would move a student out of the highest-risk group. Foundation-year grades, early credit progress, socioeconomic vulnerability and home internet access were the strongest predictors.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: Pillar 2 covers AI and predictive analytics for student success. This moves early-warning analytics from simply flagging at-risk students to prescribing specific, low-cost interventions, a model Wits AHEAD can point to for student-success work in similarly resourced settings.

Frontiers in Education · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Largest meta-analysis yet finds AI-supported STEM teaching has a real, moderate effect on learning
entry.summary:
A meta-analysis pooling 35 experimental and quasi-experimental studies has found that AI-supported instruction produces a statistically significant, moderate positive effect on STEM learning outcomes (g = 0.67). Gains were strongest for high school students, and interventions lasting one to two months proved the most effective duration tested.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: Pillar 3 covers AI and analytics in STEM and teacher education. This is among the clearest quantitative evidence yet that AI-supported STEM teaching works, and the finding on optimal intervention length is directly useful for how Wits AHEAD designs and times its own STEM programmes.

Journal of Intelligence · Peer-reviewed meta-analysis

entry.title: Gates Foundation commits 1 billion US dollars over two years to equitable AI
entry.summary:
The Gates Foundation has pledged at least 1 billion US dollars over the next two years to build and deliver equitable artificial intelligence, with 400 million earmarked for education, 400 million for health, 100 million for agriculture and 100 million for AI training data in underserved languages. The pledge accompanies the foundation's tenth Goalkeepers report, titled Make This Matter: AI, Equity and the Choice We Can't Delay.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: Pillar 6 asks who is designing AI responsibly and for whom. A philanthropic pledge of this scale, aimed at closing the gap for the poorest regions, will shape which AI-in-education tools reach the Global South classrooms Wits AHEAD studies.

Gates Foundation · Foundation press release accompanying its Goalkeepers report

entry.title: Systematic review of 105 studies finds Africa and Oceania missing from generative AI teacher research
entry.summary:
A PRISMA-guided review of 105 peer-reviewed studies on teachers and generative AI, published since 2023 in leading educational technology journals, finds the evidence base concentrated in China, Turkey, the United States and Spain, with Africa and Oceania markedly underrepresented. AI literacy, pedagogical knowledge and self-efficacy, framed through the TPACK model, are the strongest predictors of effective classroom integration, ahead of simple access to tools.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: Pillar 3 covers AI and analytics in STEM and teacher education. A review this size confirms that Wits AHEAD's own research on African teacher education fills a documented gap rather than duplicating a saturated field.

Education Sciences (MDPI) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: Stanford study finds a persistent 19% AI employment gap for young workers
entry.summary:
Stanford's Digital Economy Lab reports that employment among 22 to 25 year olds in occupations most exposed to artificial intelligence is now 19% below where it would be had it kept pace with less exposed peers, up from 15% a year earlier. The gap operates mainly through reduced hiring rather than job losses, and is concentrated in roles built on codified, textbook-taught knowledge such as software engineering and customer service.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: Pillar 4 asks how AI reshapes the route from qualification to livelihood. This is the clearest quantitative evidence yet that entry-level, knowledge-based graduate roles are narrowing first, sharpening the case for graduate capability work that goes beyond credentials.

Stanford Digital Economy Lab · University research institute report

entry.title: New Global South framework sets conditions for responsible generative AI in teaching
entry.summary:
A bibliometric and systematic review in the International Journal of Emerging Technologies in Learning traces the fast-growing literature on responsible generative AI in pedagogy and proposes a conceptual framework for the Global South. It finds research output led by the United States, China and Australia, while identifying ethical awareness, trust, institutional support, infrastructural readiness and AI competence as the conditions that most shape adoption.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: Pillar 6 covers responsible AI, ethics, equity and policy. This framework gives Wits AHEAD a peer-reviewed reference point for judging when generative AI adoption in Southern universities is genuinely responsible rather than merely available.

International Journal of Emerging Technologies in Learning (iJET) · Peer-reviewed journal article

entry.title: PISA 2025 finds 15-year-olds who skip AI chatbots for schoolwork outscore those who rely on them, as global reading skills fall sharply
entry.summary:
The OECD's PISA 2025 results, released on 8 September 2026, show reading scores falling by 28 points across OECD countries and by 16 points among other participating countries and economies between 2015 and 2025, one of the sharpest declines since the assessment began. The report finds that 15-year-olds who do not use AI chatbots for schoolwork generally score higher than those who do, and that more than one in four students say classmates are distracted by digital devices in most or every science lesson.

لماذا يهمّ AHEAD: Pillar 5, analytics and data for education systems and decision-making, gains a stark systems-level signal here: a global assessment tying heavier reliance on AI chatbots to weaker outcomes, a caution Wits AHEAD weighs directly against its own pillar 1 work on generative AI in teaching and assessment.

OECD (PISA 2025 Results, Volume I) · Intergovernmental body report
